headline: SIPRI warned of regulatory-capture risks in military AI policy as ControlAI highlighted warnings that humanity may not control AI on its 'default path,' while the UK's financial watchdog complained Meta refused joint testing of its Muse AI agent.

points.text: SIPRI examined industry engagement in military AI policy, warning of the risk of regulatory capture in multilateral policy processes and suggesting how states can mitigate it.

ControlAI highlighted warnings, including from Meta's AI chief, that it is hard to imagine humanity can maintain control over AI if development stays on the 'default path,' even as AI helps solve one of mathematics' hardest open problems.
The UK's Financial Conduct Authority complained that Meta refused a request to jointly test its Muse AI agent ahead of its UK rollout, warning of 'another force of attack' from agents.
A coalition of 42 state attorneys general moved to stop Character.AI from selling users' chat data as the company navigates bankruptcy proceedings.
